trajectory_summary: This is a disqualified orphaned-system call that the rep handled correctly at the DQ moment but then let run long as an unstructured technical Q&A. The customer was never a bookable lead — he owns a working SolarEdge system from a defunct installer and was calling out of curiosity about Ion's shingle-roofing product, not to buy anything.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown; observed outcome should be 'dq', not any booking-adjacent tag. The customer discloses an existing, working solar system with a competitor's install at 00:49, which is a hard DQ per orphaned_flow / dq_rules.ppa_existing_system-adjacent logic, and the rep himself confirms 'we're not able to work on another company's equipment' at 01:00.

observed_outcome.quote: Unfortunately, my company, we're not we're not able to work on another company's, equipment or anything like that.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Customer owns a working solar system installed by a now-defunct competitor; per orphaned_flow logic this is a hard disqualification, and the rep confirms Ion cannot service it. No appointment, callback, or booking of any kind resulted.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The customer is an existing solar owner, not a prospect for a new install, so there was never a utility-bill qualification step to run — the call was DQ'd on ownership grounds before bill collection would apply.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: My curiosity was not so much running solar. I already have that.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked 'what interested you in solar' since the intro line already presumed interest; the customer volunteered his reason unprompted (technical curiosity about an existing system), but since he isn't a prospect there was no appointment to tie the reason to.

script_coverage.quote: This is, Tyke with Ion. I received your request. You're looking at solar for the home.
Okay. Who did you, get installed with?

primary_coaching_focus.quote: Yeah. We we unfortunately, those are, like, kind of backed up right now. They're, about two years out to to order them or at least to be installed.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This is the clearest instance on the call of the rep inventing a concrete, checkable fact (a two-year backlog on an unreleased product) with no grounding — a real liability if repeated on a recorded, bookable call, and it directly violates numeric_discipline.

key_moments.quote: Unfortunately, my company, we're not we're not able to work on another company's, equipment or anything like that.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep correctly identifies the DQ but skips the actual orphaned_flow qualifying questions — own vs. lease, and whether the system is currently working — before delivering the DQ. The DQ conclusion happens to be right, but it's reached by instinct rather than by running the procedure, so it isn't fully clean.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. We we unfortunately, those are, like, kind of backed up right now. They're, about two years out to to order them or at least to be installed.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep invents a specific, unverified timeline ('about two years out') for Ion's shingle-roofing product on the spot. There is no basis in the schema or transcript for this figure — it reads as improvised filler to a curious customer rather than a grounded fact, which is a fabrication risk under numeric_discipline.

key_moments.quote: What what, just out of curiosity, what deficiency are you getting out of your panels?
key_moments.stewart_read: This is exactly the kind of technical spec question the schema flags as closer-tier content, and the rep engages with it directly (giving a panel model number) instead of using the universal escape hatch.

key_moments.quote: I'm not entirely too sure on the efficiency rating.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep admits the gap transparently rather than fabricating a number, which per knowledge_gap_handling is the better of the three response modes (dodge/admit/fabricate) — this is a small positive relative to the invented 'two years out' line eight lines earlier.
